thread:
morgan: Heads-up — putting up a small TF change to add a mixed-capacity pool for GPUs with a preemptible fallback + graceful drain tag. Trying to get buy-in before I open the PR.

hana: Can you sketch what the fallback looks like? Is this ASG mixedInstancesPolicy or Spot Fleet?

morgan: ASG mixedInstancesPolicy. Idea: primary reserved/ondemand pool + a cheaper spot/preemptible pool with lower weight and a tag that triggers a termination-handler to `kubectl drain` with 2m grace.

raj: 👍 agree on the drain. We should also emit a host tag like `eviction_grace=120` so the handler doesn't hardcode values. That makes TF idempotent.

sasha: Watch AMI rotation — if we change the LT you're going to trigger a rolling update. Need to ensure warm images for spots.

morgan: Good call. Plan is to add an immutable AMI tag on the launch template and then rotate in a canary. Will include a `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` on the LT.

carmen: For rollout, can we do a small canary in us-west-2 only? 5% of GPU capacity, monitor OOM / pod evictions for 24h.

morgan: Yep — will scope to us-west-2 first. I'll add an autoscaling group override for `desired_capacity` during canary.

raj: Terraform snippet we discussed (rough):
```hcl
resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu_spot" {
  name_prefix = "gpu-spot-"
  image_id    = var.gpu_ami
  tag_specifications = [{
    resource_type = "instance"
    tags = {
      Name = "redwood-gpu-spot"
      eviction_grace = "120"
      preemptible = "true"
    }
  }]
}

resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "gpu_mixed" {
  mixed_instances_policy = { /* instance types + weights */ }
  min_size = 0
  max_size = 50
}
```

hana: Also add a `termination_reason` metric emission from the handler so we can correlate preemptions vs normal term.

infra-bot: CI check: terraform fmt OK, tfsec warnings: 1 (IAM wildcard in module/monitoring).

morgan: I'll address tfsec separately; doesn't block this change. On the handler side, the drain flow will be: annotate instance -> handler sees tag -> `kubectl cordon` + `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120` -> after success `ec2 terminate-instance` (or let ASG replace).

carmen: Make sure the handler respects `pod disruption budgets` and falls back if PDB blocks drain. We should have a fallback: mark instance as `no-schedule` and wait 10m before forcing.

raj: One more: add a TF-managed SSM parameter for `spot_pool_weights` so ops can tweak weights without redeploy. Could be a small knob for cost tuning.

morgan: Added to my TODOs. I'll open the PR with: TF change + docs (runbook) + small argocd/helm flag to enable canary.

deploy-bot: deploy status: no ongoing deploys in us-west-2. Safe to proceed with canary.

oncall-bot: alert: last 7d spot interruptions in us-west-2 for GPU instances: 4 events (median reclaim time ~ 3m).

sasha: If median reclaim is 3m we can't rely on graceful drains for all cases. The drain is best-effort; for very short reclaims the handler should prioritize kube evict + checkpointing (where available).

morgan: Agreed. We'll treat drains as best-effort and rely on caching/replicas for resilience. Plan for PR this afternoon, tagging @eng-infra for review.

hana: Thanks — please include the Plan output and a short cost delta estimate (expected % token-hour reduction) in the PR description.

morgan: Will do.

raj: If anyone wants to prototype the handler logic: see `scripts/terminator/handler.js` — we can extend it to read `eviction_grace` tag.

carmen: 👍 will review the PR once opened. :rocket:
